topic: Who does NOT get a 1099-NEC: card/payment-app payments (1099-K), corporations (attorney exception), under $2,000, e-file at 10+ returns; due Feb 1, 2027 (LinkedIn only, Zain Nov 3)
label: 1099 season / Check
headline: Not every contractor gets a *1099-NEC*

items.title: Paid by card or app checkout?
items.text: The payment company reports it on a 1099-K. Not you.

items.title: Paid an S or C corp LLC?
items.text: Generally no 1099-NEC. Attorneys are the exception.

items.title: Under $2,000 in 2026?
items.text: Generally no form, unless you withheld backup tax.

items.title: 10+ forms in total?
items.text: You must e-file. Due Monday, Feb 1, 2027.

ig_caption:
Not every contractor you paid in 2026 gets a 1099-NEC. Before you send forms in January, check how and who you paid.

1. Paid by credit card or through a payment app's business checkout? The payment company reports it on Form 1099-K. You don't put those payments on a 1099-NEC.
2. Paid an LLC that's taxed as an S corp or C corp? Generally no 1099-NEC. The big exception: attorneys' fees are reported even when the law firm is a corporation.
3. Paid someone less than $2,000 for the year? For 2026 payments, generally no form (unless you withheld backup tax).
4. Filing 10 or more information returns in total (all 1099 types and W-2s combined)? You have to e-file them.

The 1099-NEC deadline is Monday, Feb 1, 2027, both to the contractor and to the IRS.

Quick year-end check: pull your 2026 vendor list, mark how each one was paid, and get a W-9 from anyone you still need to file for.

Source: IRS Instructions for Forms 1099-MISC and 1099-NEC. General information, not tax advice.
